proposed_comments.title: Serialize status updates through provider disposal

confidence.rationale: The host status APIs are asynchronous, and unordered show/hide/dispose work can visibly resurrect stale status UI after a provider has gone away.

proposed_comments.body:
### Serialize status updates through provider disposal

**Severity:** `high`

`ShowStatus`, `HideStatus`, provider disconnect, and provider disposal need to execute in request order. Today a hide or dispose path can race with an earlier asynchronous show, and startup notifications can interleave with live notifications before initialization has fully drained. Please serialize status host operations, track anonymous statuses as well as ID-backed statuses, and make disposal drain the queued cleanup so a disconnected JS provider cannot leave stale status UI behind.

proposed_comments.title: Fence provider publication and list-page cache updates

confidence.rationale: Reload, remove, ItemsChanged, and slow GetItems responses share mutable provider/list state; without generation checks, stale work can republish removed providers or cache invalid list adapters.

proposed_comments.body:
### Fence provider publication and list-page cache updates

**Severity:** `high`

Provider add/remove/reload and `ItemsChanged` work should be generation-fenced before publishing commands or committing list-page caches. A slow publication or completed `GetItems` response can otherwise win after a newer reload/removal and re-enable a disposed provider or stale adapter set. Please publish provider wrappers only if they are still registered for the current generation, reject invalidated list results, and release page-owned adapter caches during disposal.

proposed_comments.title: Keep crash recovery and extension removal bounded

confidence.rationale: Crash recovery and directory lifecycle gates guard the same extension directory; an unbounded wait after a timed-out recovery drain can make uninstall or hot reload hang indefinitely.

proposed_comments.body:
### Keep crash recovery and extension removal bounded

**Severity:** `high`

Crash recovery, hot reload, directory watcher work, and explicit extension removal need a single bounded ownership model for each extension directory. If recovery cancellation times out while recovery still owns the directory lifecycle gate, removal must not wait on that gate forever. Please propagate cancellation through extension task coordination, serialize load/stop decisions for a directory, route rename as remove-then-add, reset crash counts on source edits through the production path, and bound the post-recovery gate acquisition so uninstall can continue best-effort instead of hanging.

proposed_comments.title: Preserve wrapper identity and cleanup on initialization failure

confidence.rationale: Wrapper equality and failed initialization cleanup feed top-level provider bookkeeping; treating all valid wrappers as equal or leaking partially-created hosts corrupts multi-provider state.

proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve wrapper identity and cleanup on initialization failure

**Severity:** `medium`

`CommandProviderWrapper` instances should compare by reference identity, not by shared validity state. Otherwise two valid providers can collapse into the same collection entry and provider removal/reload can touch the wrong host. Please also make wrapper construction rethrow initialization failures after disposing any partially-created host so cleanup paths run consistently and failed extensions do not leave retained event handlers or host state.
